first.rationale: The competitive threat from aggressive entry pricing on price-sensitive SMB segments directly maps to memory_73's finding that targeted promotional pricing drove strong acquisition and revenue lift for that cohort. While activation and onboarding metrics are down QoQ, the immediate threat is account loss to competitor pricing—this is a revenue defense play. Memory_73 showed pricing also cut time-to-first-value, which may help address activation decline. I'm verifying memory_73 to confirm the magnitude of effect and whether the conditions still hold, and memory_86 (shortening onboarding) to understand if there's interaction potential with simpler onboarding paths that could compound benefits. Referral incentives and enterprise sales assist are lower-urgency given the immediate competitive pressure. A standard experiment on targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB cohorts balances speed of execution with sufficient sample to validate whether the prior lift still holds in current market conditions. This preserves the option to pivot to activation messaging or simplified onboarding if pricing proves insufficient.
